source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170

coverage.scope: E. Involuntary bankruptcy: petition, qualified creditors, 12-creditor test, generally not paying, gap and §303(i); F. Abstention §305; Problems 2.15–2.17
coverage.notice: 2021-book involuntary petition minimum $16,750 is indexed every 3 years and is not a current 2026 amount.

topics.title: E.1–3 — Involuntary Bankruptcy: Eligibility and Available Chapters
topics.description: Creditor-initiated Chapter 7/11, excluded debtors, why a forcible filing is rare and §303(a).

entries.title: §303 only Chapter 7 or 11
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Involuntary bankruptcy petition can be initiated by qualified creditors under Chapters 7 and 11 alone, unlike voluntary §301; no involuntary Chapters 9,12,13.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditors may force a financially distressed corporation into Chapter 7 or 11, but not an ordinary person into Chapter 13 wage-payment plan.
entries.legalExplanation: Involuntary filings historically normal but now less than 1%; proposed debtor can contest order for relief.
entries.examApplication: Check debtor class and chapter before creditor count.
entries.examTrap: Involuntary filing may create an estate and stay immediately, but order for relief is not automatic.

entries.title: §303(a) protects farmers and noncommercial corporations
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: No involuntary cases against farmer (§101(20)), family farmer (§101(18)), or corporation not 'moneyed, business, or commercial' even if chapter otherwise available.
entries.laymanExplanation: Congress protects some agricultural/charitable entities from coercive creditor filings.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish debtor type from §109 voluntary eligibility. Chapter 12 family farmers still may voluntarily petition.
entries.examApplication: Classify nonprofit corporation and farm operator.
entries.examTrap: Do not confuse Chapter 7 farmer availability voluntarily with availability involuntarily.

entries.title: Why Congress allows involuntary relief
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Protect creditor collective interest where debtor won't file despite nonpayment; danger involuntary suits themselves can damage reputations or pressure settlement.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditors can force a single orderly case instead of losing value while debtor delays.
entries.legalExplanation: 1978 Code replaced obsolete 'acts of bankruptcy' with §303(h) tests and coupled with sanctions for bad-faith petitions.
entries.examApplication: Discuss balancing group efficiency vs false threat.
entries.examTrap: Involuntary bankruptcy is not ordinary collection judgment.

topics.title: E.4 — Petitioning Creditors: Qualified Claims, Numbers and Joinder
topics.description: §303(b) noncontingent/undisputed claims, secured undercollateralized shares, threshold, three vs one petitioners and counting exclusions.

entries.title: Qualified petitioner: §303(b) claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Petitioner creditor or indenture trustee must hold prepetition claim not contingent as to liability and not subject to bona fide dispute as to liability or amount; qualifying unsecured claims aggregate to statutory indexed minimum.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditors fighting about whether any real debt exists can't use bankruptcy petition to bully debtor into paying.
entries.legalExplanation: If petitioner's claim secured, only unsecured deficiency portion may count toward unsecured aggregate. Book's minimum $16,750 is 2021 historical, not current 2026 threshold.
entries.examApplication: Check each petitioner individually for disputed/contingent claim, then total eligible unsecured dollars.
entries.examTrap: A valid judgment creditor may be qualified even if debtor refuses payment, absent bona fide dispute.

entries.title: Noncontingent vs disputed liability or amount
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: A claim contingent on event not yet occurred fails noncontingency requirement; bona fide dispute as to liability OR amount (2005 change) can disqualify; courts question if undisputed subset of amount counts.
entries.laymanExplanation: If debtor legitimately contests $1,000 of a $5,000 account, legal effect on petitioning status can be contested.
entries.legalExplanation: Textbook specifically poses open question whether admitted $4,000 portion counts or entire debt disqualified under statute.
entries.examApplication: Analyze bona fide dispute, documentation and governing circuit carefully.
entries.examTrap: Cannot silently resolve disputed-amount question with assumption in all jurisdictions.

entries.title: §303(b): three petitioners if 12+ qualifying creditors; else one
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Debtor with 12 or more eligible counted creditors requires at least 3 qualified petitioners; with fewer than 12 one qualified petitioner sufficient; petitioners must together satisfy minimum aggregate unsecured claims.
entries.laymanExplanation: If debtor owes 30 ordinary separate people, three creditors must file together; if owes 5, one may petition.
entries.legalExplanation: Each individual petitioning creditor must be qualified; not every person claiming money counts in 12-creditor denominator.
entries.examApplication: Create creditor roster and remove statutory exclusions before counting to 12.
entries.examTrap: Not 'three creditors each holding minimum dollar amount'; statute measures total unsecured petitioning claims.

entries.title: 12-creditor denominator exclusions
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: When counting 12, exclude employee creditors, insiders, transferees of voidable transfers, holders of contingent claims and bona fide disputed claimants; some courts controversially exclude tiny recurring bills.
entries.laymanExplanation: Counting to 12 is more complicated than list of every invoice, because some relationships excluded.
entries.legalExplanation: §303(b) statutory categories and Rule 1003; denominator exclusions differ from petitioning creditor predicates.
entries.examApplication: Use table of creditor, reason in/out, allowed claim.
entries.examTrap: Do not count employees/insiders as ordinary outsiders just to demand 3 signatures.

entries.title: Rule 1003 assignment prohibition and §303(c) joinder
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Claim assignee generally can't qualify as petitioner if claim assigned for purpose of filing; qualified creditors can join petition before dismissal under §303(c) and Rule 1003(b), but courts differ if initial filing in bad faith.
entries.laymanExplanation: You can't manufacture three 'creditors' by splitting one claim; late joiners may cure short petition under conditions.
entries.legalExplanation: Book mentions judicial good-faith gloss over purported technical curing.
entries.examApplication: Analyze how many originally petitioned, how many valid later joined and whether initial filer acted in good faith.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume initial shortage necessarily fatal despite timely qualified joinder.

topics.title: E.5 — Court's Order for Relief: Generally Not Paying and Custodian Alternative
topics.description: §303(h) two alternative grounds, bona fide dispute exclusion, balance-sheet vs equity insolvency, flexible nonpayment factors.

entries.title: §303(h)(1): generally not paying debts as due
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: After timely contested involuntary petition court orders relief if debtor generally not paying debts as they come due, excluding bona fide disputed debts from assessment.
entries.laymanExplanation: If business isn't paying its routine creditors broadly, forced bankruptcy may be warranted.
entries.legalExplanation: Fact-intensive analysis of number, fraction and amount unpaid, delinquency age and debtor's overall financial conduct.
entries.examApplication: For 2.15 one large judgment unpaid while 27 others current; for 2.16 most creditors unpaid except one worked-out judgment—compare size and counts.
entries.examTrap: A single $70k unpaid debt may dominate dollars but not automatically prove 'generally' unpaid.

entries.title: §303(h)(2) custodian alternative: 120 days
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Order for relief also available if qualifying custodian appointed or took possession of substantially all debtor property within 120 days before petition, subject statutory terms.
entries.laymanExplanation: Receiver or assignment for benefit of creditors recently took over most business assets; bankruptcy can supersede that collective process.
entries.legalExplanation: In fact pattern, check timing, substantially all property and whether abstention under §305 better serves estate.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish §303(h) from former old acts-of-bankruptcy triggers.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume ordinary appointment over one small asset satisfies substantially-all.

entries.title: Nonpayment equity insolvency vs balance sheet
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: §303(h)(1) asks whether debtor actually is generally paying due debts (equity insolvency concept), not whether total liabilities exceed total assets (balance-sheet insolvency).
entries.laymanExplanation: A company may own expensive real estate but still fail to pay bills this month.
entries.legalExplanation: A firm can be insolvent by asset values yet pay currently or solvent on paper yet miss most bills.
entries.examApplication: Separate cash-flow/nonpayment analysis from asset-minus-debt accounting.
entries.examTrap: Chapter 9 municipal insolvency test distinct.

entries.title: No rigid percentage test; six practical factors
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Courts weigh number of defaulted debts, percentage numerically, percentage in dollar amounts, total delinquent dollars, age of delinquencies versus industry and overall financial conduct.
entries.laymanExplanation: One big creditor vs dozens of unpaid suppliers can tell different stories.
entries.legalExplanation: The book refuses a single mathematical cutoff; §303(h) intentionally flexible.
entries.examApplication: For Problems 2.15/16 compute number unpaid and value proportions as evidence but not automatic result.
entries.examTrap: Do not decide purely by 3 of 30 or 70% of value without other factors.

entries.title: Bona fide disputes excluded from general nonpayment calculus
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Statute excludes debts that are subject to bona fide disputes as to liability or amount so creditors cannot weaponize disputed invoices.
entries.laymanExplanation: You don't count an honestly contested claim as an ignored bill for involuntary-filing pressure.
entries.legalExplanation: Debt not due, contingent and legitimately disputed differ; casebook frames debtor protection vs evasion risk.
entries.examApplication: In 2.15 judgment after litigation generally resolves earlier liability dispute, but analyze given status.
entries.examTrap: Not every debtor's subjective refusal proves 'bona fide' dispute.

topics.title: E.6 — Operations Between Filing and Order for Relief
topics.description: Gap estate/stay, debtor-in-possession rights, interim trustee, gap credit/new value, payments and Problem 2.17.

entries.title: Filing triggers automatic estate and stay despite no order yet
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Even contested involuntary petition creates §541 estate and §362 stay immediately to protect assets while court decides order for relief.
entries.laymanExplanation: Business isn't declared bankrupt yet, but creditors are paused from snatching property.
entries.legalExplanation: §303 timing: petition first, possible hearing, then order for relief or dismissal.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish filing timestamp and 'order for relief' when assessing gap transactions.
entries.examTrap: Do not presume automatic order on involuntary filing.

entries.title: §303(f): debtor may continue operation/use property in gap
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Absent court order, target of involuntary case may continue operating business and using property during contested gap; §303(g) court may appoint interim trustee to prevent loss.
entries.laymanExplanation: Airline usually keeps flying scheduled routes while court decides whether bankruptcy forced.
entries.legalExplanation: Court can require petitioner bond §303(e), interim trustee if needed; property turnover via debtor bond.
entries.examApplication: Problem 2.17(a) airline flights after Dec 20 involuntary filing.
entries.examTrap: Operating business doesn't mean lawful to pay every old debt.

entries.title: §303(g) interim trustee and bond
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Court may appoint interim trustee when needed to preserve estate or prevent loss, and debtor may regain possession by posting bond.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge can put someone in charge if debtor is dissipating assets during contest.
entries.legalExplanation: Even without full relief order, special protection of estate can be implemented.
entries.examApplication: Look for evidence business cash disappearing versus ordinary operation.
entries.examTrap: Interim appointment isn't automatic merely on petition.

entries.title: Gap financing and priority §502(f),§507(a)(3)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Credit extended in ordinary course during gap may receive statutory priority in case eventually adjudicated; third priority in textbook discussion.
entries.laymanExplanation: Food supplier may keep feeding flights with special protection for new deliveries.
entries.legalExplanation: Differentiate debt incurred before involuntary petition from postpetition gap credit and split mixed invoices by delivery date.
entries.examApplication: For 2.17(c) $50k invoice straddles Dec15–Jan15; classify each portion by when goods delivered.
entries.examTrap: Don't treat mixed-date invoice as one single prepetition or postpetition debt.

entries.title: §549 gap transfers, prepetition debt payments and new value
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Prepetition claims generally cannot be selectively paid during gap without avoidance risk; under §549(b) transferees giving new value during gap get protection to value given.
entries.laymanExplanation: Old bill payments may be clawed back; fresh goods delivered for new payment get different treatment.
entries.legalExplanation: §549(b) protects new-value transfers under specified requirements, not unconditional permission for all distributions.
entries.examApplication: For 2.17(b) Jan1 wage payment, determine whether earned pre-Dec20 vs after; for supplier divide before/after Dec20.
entries.examTrap: No blanket permission to pay antecedent claims because Chapter 11-like ordinary operation continues.

topics.title: E.7 and F — Dismissal, §303(i) Sanctions and §305 Abstention
topics.description: False involuntary filing costs and penalties; collective posture even after petitioners consent to withdrawal; out-of-court workout abstention.

entries.title: §303(j): involuntary petition can't always be dismissed by parties alone
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Court may dismiss for petitioners' failure to prove grounds, consent, want of prosecution, or abstention, but must protect body of creditors when petitioners/debtor agree to withdrawal.
entries.laymanExplanation: Involuntary case affects everyone, not just original three creditors; their private deal doesn't always end it.
entries.legalExplanation: §303(j) requires statutory process with notice/hearing protection before consent dismissal.
entries.examApplication: If petitioners settle privately, ask if other creditors could be harmed.
entries.examTrap: Do not treat involuntary petition like ordinary two-party voluntary civil dismissal.

entries.title: §303(i) fees, compensatory and punitive damages
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: If involuntary case dismissed outside specified consent exceptions, court may award costs and reasonable attorneys' fees; if petitioners acted in bad faith court may award proximately caused damages and punitive damages.
entries.laymanExplanation: Wrongful creditor-forced bankruptcy can be financially costly for petitioners.
entries.legalExplanation: §303(i)(1) costs/fees; §303(i)(2) actual and punitive damages if bad faith. §303(e) petitioner's bond may secure.
entries.examApplication: Separate baseline fee recovery from heightened bad-faith sanctions.
entries.examTrap: Punitive damages not automatic simply because involuntary petition failed.

entries.title: §305(a)(1): abstention when better for debtor and creditors
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Even legally valid bankruptcy can be dismissed/suspended if interests of creditors and debtor better served by nonbankruptcy arrangement; discretionary court determination.
entries.laymanExplanation: A negotiated restructuring could work better than bankruptcy if it protects all affected creditors.
entries.legalExplanation: Classic: minority holdout threatening involuntary filing to extract payment despite fair, cheaper workout supported by others.
entries.examApplication: Compare collective efficiency, cost, consent, creditor risk, prejudice and timing.
entries.examTrap: Abstention is not finding debtor ineligible or petitioners lacked cause.

entries.title: In re Colonial Ford voluntary-case abstention example
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
entries.summary: Book cites Colonial Ford: car dealership had comprehensive pre-bankruptcy creditor workout with nine months to sell/refinance then foreclosure; debtor failed and filed Chapter 11 to delay agreed foreclosure; court abstained.
entries.laymanExplanation: After agreeing to a good outside workout, debtor can't always use Chapter 11 as endless delay.
entries.legalExplanation: Case appears as described example, not full opinion excerpt; illustrates §305 even voluntary case.
entries.examApplication: Discuss why court would respect prior arm's-length workout.
entries.examTrap: Do not describe it as full brief or universal rule that every workout bars filing.

problems.title: Problem 2.15
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
problems.prompt: Three petitioners Alpha ($70k final undisputed judgment), Beta ($100), Gamma ($100), 30 creditors and $100k total debts; only petitioners unpaid; decide whether generally not paying under §303(h)(1), including creditor count and dollar ratios. Unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 2.16
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
problems.prompt: Three petitioners Beta/Gamma/Delta each undisputed $5k; 30 creditors, $100k debt; all creditors unpaid except Alpha on a $90k judgment after $20k payment and installment schedule for $70k remainder. Determine §303(h)(1) general nonpayment from numeric and value proportions, without solving.

problems.title: Problem 2.17
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, Fifth Edition (2021), full uploaded Chapter 2 §§E–F; Effross Fall 2026 syllabus general pp.79–170
problems.prompt: Gap period airline hypothetical: creditors file involuntary case Dec20; (a) scheduled holiday flights, (b) Jan1 $1m wages, (c) $50k inflight meals invoice Jan15 for services Dec15 through Jan15. Distinguish ordinary business operation, prepetition/postpetition portions, new value and statutory priority, all unanswered.
